sentence: The NHS says people can buy a monitor to check blood pressure at home, using an upper arm cuff, sitting relaxed and avoiding caffeine and smoking first.
note: NHS: can buy your own BP machine; upper arm cuff; seated and relaxed; no caffeine/smoke 30 min

sentence: High blood pressure does not usually cause symptoms, so measuring it is the way to find out.
note: High blood pressure does not usually have any symptoms

sentence: Blood pressure is written as two numbers, the first higher than the second.
note: Two numbers, first higher than second

sentence: NHS-linked guidance recommends an upper arm monitor rather than a wrist or finger device.
note: Finger and/or wrist BP devices are not recommended

sentence: A single high reading is usually not a cause for alarm, and a GP or nurse decides the schedule and target.
note: Single high reading usually not cause for alarm; GP or nurse decides schedule and target

sentence: The NHS says a blood pressure test can check whether blood pressure is too high or too low.
note: Test can check if blood pressure too high or too low

sentence: High blood pressure does not usually have any symptoms, while low blood pressure can cause dizziness or fainting.
note: High usually no symptoms; low can cause dizziness or fainting

sentence: Readings are given as two numbers with the first higher than the second; the top figure is the pressure as the heart pumps and the bottom is the lowest pressure between beats.
note: Two numbers; systolic when heart pumps; diastolic lowest between beats

sentence: The NHS says people can use their own device, and that a blood pressure machine can be bought for home use.
note: Can buy your own blood pressure machine to use at home

sentence: NHS England has a programme of home blood pressure monitoring through GP practices.
note: NHS England home blood pressure monitoring (page title and 2021 news)

sentence: The NHS says blood pressure is usually considered high at a lower figure when checked at home than when checked by a healthcare professional.
Local NHS guides recommend an automatic upper arm monitor with a cuff that fits snugly, and say that wrist and finger devices are not recommended.
note: Upper arm cuff; finger and wrist devices not recommended; cuff should fit upper arm snugly

sentence: They describe sitting quietly for about five minutes with feet flat and the back supported, and avoiding caffeine, smoking, exercise and eating for about 30 minutes beforehand.
note: Sit quietly five minutes; avoid caffeine, smoking, exercise and eating for 30 minutes

sentence: Readings are usually taken twice in the morning and twice in the evening over about a week, with the average worked out afterwards.
note: Two readings morning and evening over about a week; average calculated

sentence: The guides advise taking readings before blood pressure tablets and leaving at least a minute between two readings.
note: Take readings before any blood pressure tablets; two readings at least a minute apart

sentence: One guide recommends choosing a monitor validated by the British and Irish Hypertension Society.
note: Look for device validated by BIHSOC

sentence: The NHS says the GP or nurse decides the schedule and the target for each person.
note: Your GP or nurse decides the schedule and your target

sentence: One guide notes that a single high reading is usually not a cause for alarm and that it can be retaken later.
note: A single high reading is usually not cause for alarm, so retake it later

sentence: Readings that are consistently high are a reason to contact the GP practice, according to one NHS integrated care board page, and very high readings with symptoms need same-day advice from NHS 111 or the GP practice.
note: Contact your GP practice if readings consistently high; Sussex: average 170/115 or above same day GP or NHS 111
